title: Actor-head low-LR convergence tail
benchmark: A frozen learned policy plays at least 100,000 fresh 200bb HUNL Slumbot hands, scores above 0 bb/100, and has a 95% confidence-interval lower bound above 0.
hypothesis: The current strongest external candidate may be under-converged: preserving its exact Adam moments and terminal 1e-5 learning rate for a disjoint second 131k physical-hand segment can improve greedy policy strength without the destructive drift observed in earlier full-network scale-ups.
material_change: Resume the exact raw actor-head checkpoint without resetting optimizer, legacy hand counter, EMA, adaptive-league state, or assignment RNG; use disjoint fixed-deal indices from 132553 and hold LR at the inherited 1e-5 until 262144 physical lineage hands. Evaluate only as a convergence mechanism gate before any fresh Slumbot allocation.
baseline: v6-actor-ema-terminal-smoke-20260831 frozen raw endpoint; greedy fresh5k -9.4188 bb/100 CI crossing zero

Evidence limitation found by independent review: a recovery evaluation-loop path mistakenly overwrote execution.json with a stale recovery snapshot. The authoritative recovery_execution.json is complete; the zero-hand startup failure remains evidenced by immutable train_stdout.log/failure.txt, the recorded first trainer command lacking --no-reset-optimizer, the corrected exact command containing it, and parent checkpoint/prefix hashes. The bug was patched before review; no model, hand, matrix, or decision artifact changed.

result.summary: Optimizer-continuous low-LR actor tail reached 263022 physical lineage hands and passed its internal greedy convergence gate; independent evidence review passed with a documented stale execution-snapshot limitation.
result.conclusion: A second 130469-hand segment materially improved the candidate over its parent on the training-opponent greedy matrix (+46.37 bb/100, paired CI lower +7.50, 4/5 anchors positive). This is not generalization evidence, but it justifies the preregistered independent fresh5k Slumbot pilot.
